texts.preamble: Samiulla Khan vs The State Of Telangana And 3 Others on 8 February, 2021 Author: K.Lakshman Bench: K.Lakshman The Hon'Ble Sri Justice K.Lakshman Writ Petition No.19607 of 2020 Order:
texts.facts: 2. The petitioner is accused in Cr.No.106 of 2020 of Adilabad Rural Police Station, Adilabad District. The offences registered against him are under Sections 270 and 273 read with 34 of IPC and Section 20 (2) read with 7(2) of Cigarette & Tobacco Product Act, 2003 (for short 'COTPA Act'). 3.
texts.arguments: Learned counsel for the petitioner as well as the learned Government Pleader for Home would submit that the subject matter is squarely covered by a common order in Chidurala Shyamsubder v. State of Telangana1 rendered by the High Court of Judicature at Hyderabad for the State of Telangana and the State of Andhra Pradesh, and placed copy of the said judgment for perusal. 4. In Chidurala Shyamsubder's case (supra), a learned Single Judge of the High Court, following the guidelines laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal2, held that the Police are incompetent to take cognizance of the offences punishable under Sections 45 and 59(1) of the Food Safety and Standards (FSS) Act, 2006, investigating into the offences along with other Samiulla Khan vs The State Of Telangana And 3 Others on 8 February, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87633210/ 1 offences under the provisions of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, and filing charge sheet is grave illegality, as the Food Officer alone is competent to investigate and to file charge sheet following the Rules laid down under Sections 41 and 42 of FSS Act, whereas, in the present case, the Police have registered the crime for the offences under Sections under Sections 270 and 273 read with 34 of IPC and Section 20 (2) read with 7(2) of the COTPA Act. 6. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner that the seized property is in the custody of Adilabad Rural Police Station, Adilabad District and sought direction to the Adilabad Police Station, Adilabad District, to return the seized property to the petitioner.
texts.petitioner_arguments: Learned counsel for the petitioner as well as the learned Government Pleader for Home would submit that the subject matter is squarely covered by a common order in Chidurala Shyamsubder v. State of Telangana1 rendered by the High Court of Judicature at Hyderabad for the State of Telangana and the State of Andhra Pradesh, and placed copy of the said judgment for perusal.
texts.respondent_arguments: 6. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner that the seized property is in the custody of Adilabad Rural Police Station, Adilabad District and sought direction to the Adilabad Police Station, Adilabad District, to return the seized property to the petitioner.
texts.other_lawyer_arguments: 4.
